target_customer: Independent creatives and later wedding and event businesses such as photographers, planners, venues and caterers
problem: Small creative and event businesses juggle leads, quotes, contracts, invoices and contractor payments across separate tools. Maroo bundles CRM with payments.
business_model: SaaS plus payments; free plan with zero fee ACH and cards, revenue from payments and paid tiers
product_category: CRM and payments for creative and event businesses

founders.name: Alex Nikityuk
founders.background_notes: Finance leader who says he led a 500M fundraise at Revolut, per the YC page.

founders.name: Andrei Riaskov
founders.background_notes: Background in CRM building and enterprise software.

founders.name: Anja Winikka
founders.background_notes: 13 years at The Knot Worldwide in digital marketing and content.

technical_complexity.rationale: CRM is standard, but moving money via ACH and cards, 1099 filing and QuickBooks sync add compliance and integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Stored client records and payment flows create some lock in, but the vertical software category was crowded and features copyable.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not found as of founding; the company was acquired by a holding company in 2026 rather than displaced.

market_need_then: Not evidenced by a dated source in this research; the product later narrowed to wedding and event businesses.

branding.domain_note: Uses maroo.us rather than maroo.com; legal entity shown as Ooram Inc.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain pitch around zero fees and free CRM

brand_strength.rationale: Little press on the brand beyond acquisition coverage, and the name collides with Maroo AI and the similar Marloo.

pivots.to: business management and payments platform for wedding and event businesses
pivots.why: Not stated; inferred from YC description versus current site and press releases

outcome_analysis: Maroo started as a CRM for creatives out of YC Summer 2021, took a small pre-seed round and total funding reported near 3.8 to 3.96 million dollars, and narrowed toward wedding and event businesses with payments. It was acquired by Helium Ventures in April 2026 with terms undisclosed. The company claims over 13,000 to 15,000 businesses on the platform, which suggests a modest but real small business footprint.
notes: Total raised: press release says 3.8M from YC, Pioneer Fund, Acrobator; CB Insights says 3.96M over 6 rounds. Only the 2021-06 pre-seed date is sourced (Crunchbase, no amount); other rounds not itemized. Competitor search returned only 2025 and 2026 comparison articles, so no dated competitor list was recorded. The 13,000 and 15,000 customer figures come from the press release and company site and differ. Pivot date unknown.
